heading: Oregon Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Oregon paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Oregon income tax, Social Security, Medicare, Paid Leave Oregon contributions, statewide transit tax and applicable local deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Oregon has several distinctive payroll deductions that can affect take-home income, particularly for employees living or working in the Portland metropolitan area.

Whether you work in Portland, Salem, Eugene, Bend or another Oregon community, understanding your net earnings can help you compare employment opportunities and establish realistic financial goals.

## How to Use the Oregon Paycheck Calculator

Choose annual salary or hourly wages and enter your earnings before taxes.

Select your payment frequency. Enter the federal and Oregon income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Enter applicable Oregon local income tax in the local withholding field. Under Benefits, open Advanced settings and enter the total of your employee Paid Leave Oregon, statewide transit tax and Workers' Benefit Fund deductions under Other deductions. Enter each deduction once.

Enter prior year-to-date taxable wages if you are approaching a Social Security or Additional Medicare threshold.

Review your estimated gross earnings, individual deductions and remaining take-home pay.

Use your latest pay stub to confirm which local taxes and insurance contributions apply.

## Oregon Payroll Taxes in 2026

The [Oregon Department of Revenue payroll information page](https://www.oregon.gov/dor/programs/businesses/pages/payroll-updates.aspx) provides official formulas, withholding tables and annual updates.

## How Oregon State Income Tax Works

Oregon uses progressive individual income tax rates of 4.75%, 6.75%, 8.75% and 9.9%.

However, employers do not simply apply these percentages to gross wages.

Oregon's payroll calculation accounts for applicable standard deductions, withholding allowances and a deduction for eligible federal income tax withholding.

The applicable federal tax deduction is subject to limits and income-related adjustments.

For 2026, the standard amounts used in the employer withholding formulas are $2,910 for the applicable single classification and $5,820 for the applicable married or higher-allowance classification.

The official calculation also incorporates an annual allowance credit of $263 where applicable.

Review the [2026 Oregon Withholding Tax Formulas](https://www.oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/withholding-tax-formulas_206-436_2026.pdf) for the complete methodology.

## Understanding Oregon Form OR-W-4

Oregon employees generally complete Form OR-W-4 to communicate their withholding information.

This form is separate from federal Form W-4.

The number of allowances, marital classification and additional withholding requested by an employee can affect state income tax deductions.

Employees with multiple jobs, working spouses or additional income should review their withholding elections carefully.

The official [2026 OR-W-4 instructions](https://www.oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/form-or-w-4-instr_101-402-1_2026.pdf) explain how to determine appropriate allowances.

## Oregon Statewide Transit Tax

Oregon imposes a statewide transit tax on applicable employee wages.

The rate remains 0.1% in 2026. A proposed increase was rejected by voters in May 2026.

The tax generally applies to wages earned by Oregon residents and wages earned by nonresidents performing services within Oregon, subject to applicable exclusions.

Employees may owe statewide transit tax even if their ordinary Oregon income tax withholding is zero.

Do not confuse this employee deduction with TriMet or Lane Transit District employer payroll taxes.

Visit the official [Oregon statewide transit tax guidance](https://www.oregon.gov/dor/programs/businesses/Pages/statewide-transit-tax.aspx) for details.

## Paid Leave Oregon Contributions

Paid Leave Oregon provides qualifying workers with partial income replacement during eligible periods of family, medical or safe leave.

For 2026, the total standard contribution rate is 1% of covered wages.

Employees generally pay 60% of that amount, equivalent to 0.6% of covered earnings. Employers may choose to cover the employee's contribution.

The annual covered wage ceiling is $184,500 per employer.

The maximum standard annual employee contribution is therefore:

$184,500 × 0.006 = $1,107.

For an employee receiving $2,500 in covered wages before reaching the annual limit, the ordinary employee contribution is $15.

Read the official [Paid Leave Oregon employee guidance](https://paidleave.oregon.gov/employees/overview.html) for information about contributions, eligibility and benefits.

## Oregon Workers' Benefit Fund Assessment

Oregon also collects an hourly assessment to support programs for injured workers and their families.

The total assessment rate is 1.8 cents per hour worked in 2026.

Under ordinary equal cost-sharing arrangements, the employee share is 0.9 cents per applicable hour.

For an employee working 80 covered hours during a biweekly pay period:

80 × $0.009 = $0.72.

This contribution is based on applicable working hours rather than a percentage of salary.

Consult the [Oregon Workers' Benefit Fund](https://www.oregon.gov/dcbs/wbf/pages/index.aspx) for official assessment information.

## Portland and Other Oregon Local Income Taxes

Employees living or working in the Portland metropolitan area may encounter additional local income taxes.

These can include the Metro Supportive Housing Services income tax and Multnomah County's Preschool for All income tax.

Each program has separate jurisdiction, income threshold and withholding requirements.

Portland also administers an Arts Tax, which should not automatically be treated as an ordinary payroll withholding deduction.

Employees working in Eugene may encounter its Community Safety Payroll Tax.

Do not apply Portland-area taxes to every Oregon employee.

Review the [Portland Revenue Division](https://www.portland.gov/revenue) and [City of Eugene tax resources](https://www.eugene-or.gov/) for applicable local requirements.

## Oregon Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Suppose you earn $28 per hour and work 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings: $28 × 40 = $1,120.

Overtime earnings: $28 × 1.5 × 6 = $252.

Total gross earnings: $1,372.

Paid Leave Oregon would ordinarily deduct $8.23, while statewide transit tax would deduct approximately $1.37, assuming all wages are covered and the applicable annual contribution ceiling has not been reached.

Other federal, state and local deductions may also apply.

Review the [Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries](https://www.oregon.gov/boli/workers/pages/default.aspx) for wage and overtime requirements.

## Federal Taxes on Oregon Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding follows the procedures in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered wages up to $184,500 in 2026, while ordinary Medicare applies at 1.45%.

Additional Medicare withholding may apply above the employer's $200,000 annual wage threshold.

Review the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and [Social Security contribution limits](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html) for further information.

## Working in Oregon and Living in Washington

Washington does not impose individual income tax on ordinary wages. However, Washington residents working in Oregon may still owe Oregon income tax on qualifying Oregon-sourced earnings.

Living across the Columbia River does not automatically eliminate Oregon payroll withholding.

Remote work and employment across state lines may require additional income allocation calculations.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Oregon's statewide transit tax rate in 2026?

The statewide transit tax remains 0.1% of applicable employee wages following the rejection of the proposed increase in May 2026.

### How much does Paid Leave Oregon deduct from employee paychecks?

The standard employee contribution is 0.6% of covered wages up to $184,500 per employer in 2026.

### Do all Oregon employees pay Portland-area income taxes?

No. Metro, Multnomah County and other local taxes depend on applicable residence, employment, income thresholds and withholding requirements.

## Calculate Your Oregon Take-Home Pay

Use our Oregon paycheck calculator to understand how taxes and payroll contributions affect your earnings.

Combine your estimated net income with our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) and [loan payment calculator](/calculators/loan-calculator/) to create a realistic financial plan.
